scope: OLP-0607 distributivity of union over intersection via nested case proofs; state-only draft

additional_semantic_checks: The proposition is exactly A union (B intersection C) equals (A union B) intersection (A union C), for arbitrary A, B and C.
Equality is unpacked as two set inclusions. The first direction takes arbitrary z in A union (B intersection C) and splits into z in A or z in B intersection C.
First-direction Case 1 obtains membership in both unions from z in A; Case 2 obtains the two unions separately from z in B and z in C.
The reverse direction resets the first-direction assumptions despite reusing variable z. It first splits z in A or z in B, then within z in B splits z in A or z in C.
Nested Case 2a does not need the z in B assumption; Case 2b uses z in B and z in C to obtain B intersection C.
All fifteen pedagogical quote environments remain distinct from the proof steps, and three logical-or words inside set-builder math are localized without changing formulas.
